{"candidate_slot":1,"current_prompt":"You are given a JSON object with two inputs: 'system_profile' (installed software inventory with product names and versions) and 'advisories' (a supplied list of CVE entries, each with an ID, a description, and affected-product/version information). Determine which SUPPLIED advisories apply to the installed system and return only their IDs.

Return ONLY a JSON object of the form: {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} where the array contains unique identifiers copied verbatim from the supplied advisory list. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Do NOT include any other text, explanation, or formatting.

CRITICAL BIAS WARNING: In this task, MISSING an applicable advisory is the most common and most costly error. When in doubt after a genuine product-name match, lean toward INCLUDING the advisory, provided the version is not clearly outside the range. Systematically check EVERY advisory against EVERY installed product before excluding anything.

Matching rules — follow ALL of them carefully:

1. Only use the supplied advisories. Never output a CVE ID not present in the supplied 'advisories' list. Never invent or guess CVE IDs.

2. Product-name matching must be EXHAUSTIVE and GENEROUS.
   - Normalize BOTH sides before comparing: lowercase; convert underscores, hyphens, and dots to spaces; strip vendor/organization prefixes packaging systems add (e.g. 'vendor_libx' vs 'libx'); strip common suffixes like '_package', '-lib', version suffixes; collapse repeated separators; also compare title case, snake case, kebab case, spaced forms, and repo-style names.
   - Matching is case-insensitive and separator-insensitive. If ANY alias of the advisory's affected product name matches ANY alias of ANY installed product, treat the product as installed and proceed to version checking.
   - Check the advisory's structured affected-product field(s) AND any product names given in the description. Some advisories identify the affected product only in prose or use a differently styled name; a product mentioned in the advisory's own affected information (fields or description, e.g. 'affects foo before 2.0') counts as the affected product. Do NOT restrict yourself to one field — reconcile all product identifiers present in the advisory.
   - Partial/core-name overlap counts: if the normalized core tokens of the names are the same, it is a match. A mismatch in surface form alone is NEVER a valid reason to rule out an advisory.

3. Version comparison is the main decision point. Parse BOTH structured fields and prose carefully ('affected', 'less_than', 'greater_than', ranges, 'fixed_in', 'affects versions prior to X', 'up to and including Y', 'fixed in Z', 'X and later', 'X through Y'). If structured fields and prose conflict, prefer the interpretation that makes the bounds consistent and inclusive of boundary versions.
   - INCLUSIVE BOUNDARIES COUNT. A version exactly ON an inclusive end bound ('up to and including', 'through', inclusive range end) IS affected. A lower bound 'from X' / 'X and later' / '>= X' includes X itself.
   - LOWER BOUNDS — check first, but do not over-apply. If the advisory states a lower bound, an installed version strictly BELOW it does not apply. BUT many advisories have NO lower bound ('before X', 'fixed in X', 'less_than X'). For these, ANY version below X applies — including very old versions (0.x, 1.0, 2.3.1). Explicitly ask: 'Does this advisory state a lower bound at all?' If not, the range starts at 0.0. Never exclude an old version for being 'too old' when no lower bound is stated.
   - UPPER BOUNDS AND FIXES. A version at or above a fix version ('fixed in Z', 'fixed_in') is NOT affected. 'less_than X' or 'prior to X' means installed < X applies; a version exactly equal to X with an EXCLUSIVE marker ('less than', 'prior to', 'before') is NOT affected — this is the only boundary case that excludes.
   - If NO upper bound and NO fix version is stated, the range is unbounded above: any version at or above the lower bound applies.
   - Write out the resolved inequality for every matched pair before deciding: 'before X' → installed < X; 'after X' → installed > X; 'from X through Y' → X <= installed <= Y; 'fixed in Z' → installed < Z; 'X and later' → installed >= X. Substitute the installed version.
   - Compare versions NUMERICALLY segment by segment, zero-padding to equal length (1.2.10 > 1.2.9; 1.10 > 1.9; 2.0 == 2; 1.2 == 1.2.0). NEVER compare as strings. Handle versions with 1, 2, 3, or more segments.

4. Do not exclude on product-name grounds when the product IS installed. Perform a FULL cross-product pass: check EVERY installed product against EVERY advisory, using all aliases on both sides, before ruling out any advisory as unrelated.

5. Do not include advisories whose affected product is genuinely absent from the system profile. However, a related product mentioned within the advisory's own affected information (fields or description naming it as affected) CAN be the affected product — check whether that name aliases to an installed product. The version must also fall inside the affected range. Mere ecosystem or vendor mentions with no version-relevant product match are unrelated.

6. Deduplicate: each applicable advisory ID appears at most once. IDs must be copied verbatim. Order does not matter.

Procedure — execute every step in order; show nothing of the intermediate work in the output:
- Step A: For EACH installed product, list all aliases (package-manager name, underscore form, spaced form, vendor-stripped form, title case, repo-style name).
- Step B: For EACH advisory, list all aliases of its affected product name(s) from ALL fields and the description, then compare alias sets case-insensitively against EVERY installed product's alias set. Record every (installed product, advisory) pair whose alias sets intersect. Never skip on name style.
- Step C: For each matched pair, extract BOTH bounds and their inclusivity. Decide inclusivity from explicit markers: 'up to and including', 'through', 'inclusive' → inclusive; 'prior to', 'before', 'less than' → exclusive upper; 'from', 'starting with', 'greater than or equal', 'X and later' → inclusive lower; 'greater than', 'after' → exclusive lower. If no lower bound is stated anywhere, start the range at 0.0. If no upper bound is stated, the range is unbounded above.
- Step D: Rewrite each range as a concrete inequality. Zero-pad and compare segment-wise numerically against BOTH bounds. Include the advisory if and only if the product matches AND the inequality holds.
- Step E: Collect matching advisory IDs, deduplicate, and emit the JSON object. Final audit, both directions, for every matched pair: (a) versions exactly ON inclusive bounds were INCLUDED; (b) versions strictly below a stated lower bound were EXCLUDED; (c) versions above an exclusive upper bound or at/above a fix version were EXCLUDED; (d) versions below the upper bound with NO stated lower bound were INCLUDED, even if very old; (e) no product was ruled out on name style alone; (f) EVERY advisory whose product matched and whose version satisfies the inequality appears in the output — re-scan the advisory list one final time to confirm nothing applicable was missed; (g) no ID outside the supplied list was emitted.

Return ONLY the final JSON object with the key
